content.user_title: Plan Cross-Border Financing and Offshore Issuance
content.value_statement: Cross-border financing requires coordinated decisions across several regulatory systems. This skill compares routes and structures a compliance-focused project plan.
actual_capabilities: Compares offshore debt, offshore listing, cross-border ABS, secured financing, and QFLP or QDLP routes.
Maps foreign exchange, data transfer, securities, and foreign-law compliance gates.
Organizes an eleven-stage workflow from route selection through ongoing management.
Creates draft checklists for filings, intermediaries, due diligence, settlement, and disclosure.
Compares CIPS, SWIFT, MT700, cash pools, and NRA or FT accounts.
Identifies dependencies involving asset ownership, cash flow, valuation, SPV structure, KYC, and AML.
limitations: The skill does not provide licensed legal, tax, securities, or investment advice.
Its regulatory references lack sufficient official citations and require independent verification.
It cannot submit filings, establish entities, transfer funds, or contact regulators.
Timelines and route suitability depend on current rules, facts, jurisdictions, and licensed adviser review.

use_cases.title: Screen Financing Routes
use_cases.description: Compare five financing structures against asset quality, funding goals, timeline, and compliance constraints.

use_cases.title: Build a Compliance Workplan
use_cases.description: Map filings, data transfer reviews, foreign exchange registrations, advisers, and decision gates.

use_cases.title: Design Settlement Operations
use_cases.description: Evaluate settlement tools and document the required banking, account, and funds-flow decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Available Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the five cross-border financing routes for a Chinese company. Compare purpose, prerequisites, complexity, and major compliance gates.

prompt_templates.title: Shortlist Suitable Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these assets and funding goals: [details]. Shortlist suitable routes, explain exclusions, identify missing facts, and state assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Compliance Workplan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased workplan for [route] involving [jurisdictions]. Cover filings, foreign exchange, data transfer, securities law, advisers, evidence, and decision gates.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge an Offshore Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Red-team this proposed structure: [details]. Test ownership, cash flows, SPV control, data transfers, KYC, AML, settlement, disclosure, and regulatory assumptions.

output_examples.input: Compare offshore debt and cross-border ABS for a registered data asset with recurring revenue.
output: Preliminary fit: cross-border ABS may align better with recurring asset cash flows.
Key evidence: ownership registration, enforceable contracts, cash-flow history, valuation, and transfer restrictions.
Decision gates: verified issuance authority, data transfer scope, foreign exchange registration, and licensed counsel review.
Open questions: funding currency, investor jurisdiction, recourse, credit enhancement, and intended settlement route.

output_examples.input: Prepare a workplan for a Hong Kong SPV financing structure.
output: Phase 1: confirm asset ownership, funding purpose, jurisdictions, and regulated activities.
Phase 2: validate the SPV, tax, accounting, securities, foreign exchange, and data transfer analysis.
Phase 3: appoint licensed advisers and prepare verified filing, diligence, KYC, AML, and disclosure materials.
Phase 4: approve settlement flows, closing conditions, reporting duties, and ongoing compliance ownership.

best_practices: Verify every rule against current official sources and record the verification date.
Give licensed advisers complete facts about assets, parties, jurisdictions, data, funds, and investors.
Treat foreign exchange, data, securities, and foreign-law reviews as independent approval gates.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on unnamed internal materials as final legal authority.
Do not choose a route before confirming ownership, cash flows, investor jurisdiction, and funding purpose.
Do not move data or funds before required assessments, registrations, filings, and approvals are complete.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It organizes issues and draft plans for review by qualified legal, tax, banking, and regulatory advisers.

faq.question: Which financing routes does it compare?
faq.answer: It covers offshore debt, offshore listings, cross-border ABS or tokenization, secured financing, and QFLP or QDLP channels.

faq.question: Can it confirm that a tokenized issuance is permitted?
faq.answer: No. Applicable permissions require current official sources, complete transaction facts, and advice from licensed counsel in each jurisdiction.

faq.question: Does every project require a data transfer filing?
faq.answer: No. The requirement depends on whether regulated data crosses borders, its type, volume, recipients, purpose, and applicable exemptions.

faq.question: Can it recommend a settlement method?
faq.answer: It can compare common tools, but banks and advisers must confirm account eligibility, controls, currency rules, and operational feasibility.

faq.question: What information improves the analysis?
faq.answer: Provide asset ownership, cash flows, valuation, funding purpose, parties, jurisdictions, investor type, data flows, currency, timeline, and existing approvals.
